purpose: One truthful baseline install, typecheck, build and API boot in the cell the repository itself declares. This is a measurement of the acquired application, not an attempt to make anything pass.

declaredByRepository.packageManagerDeclared: none; no packageManager field. yarn is implied by the committed yarn.lock, the .yarnrc file and every script in package.json.
declaredByRepository.coherence: The .nvmrc pin, the .node-version pin and the CI container all name Node 14; engines allows anything from 12 up.

used.platform: darwin-x64 executed on darwin-arm64 through Rosetta 2
used.translationRequiredNote: Node 14 has no darwin-arm64 build, so honouring the repository's own pin on this host requires translation. This is a property of the host, not of the application.
used.packageManager: yarn 1.22.22, installed into a scratch global prefix using the npm 6.14.12 bundled with the pinned Node runtime
used.honestLabel: exact-pin: Node 14.16.1 is the version the repository names in both .nvmrc and .node-version. No deviation was needed and none was taken.

steps.detail: yarn accepted the committed lockfile under --frozen-lockfile, so the closure installed is the closure the repository pins. 1463 top-level entries in node_modules. Twelve pre-existing peer-dependency warnings and five resolutions-field incompatibility warnings; no errors.

steps.command: tsc --noEmit (the repository's own `yarn types`, which is also its prebuild hook and its husky pre-push hook)
steps.detail: Clean. No diagnostics against typescript 4.3.4 over the full src/, backend/, scripts/ and cypress/ surface.

artifact.shape: a CRA 4 production bundle: runtime-main chunk, a main chunk and roughly thirty numbered code-split chunks, plus hashed CSS, the public assets and asset-manifest.json

steps.environmentNote: CI was cleared for this step. create-react-app promotes lint warnings to errors when CI is truthy, which would report a lint outcome as a compile outcome; the build is recorded here as a compile result.
steps.detail: webpack 4.44.2 completed with no compile error. This is the first React fixture in the corpus whose baseline build produced an artifact on the first attempt with zero deviations.

steps.command: ts-node -P tsconfig.tsnode.json --files backend/app.ts (the repository's own `yarn start:api`, minus the nyc coverage wrapper)
steps.detail: The in-repo Express + lowdb API bound its declared loopback port and served real responses.
prerequisitesRun: cp data/database-seed.json data/database.json  — the repository's own db:seed:dev / prestart step
cp scripts/mock-aws-exports.js src/aws-exports.js  — the repository's own copy:mock:awsexports / predev:cognito:ci step
cp scripts/mock-aws-exports-es5.js aws-exports-es5.js  — the repository's own copy:mock:awsexportses5 step
steps.prerequisiteFinding: Without the mock-aws-exports step the server does not start at all: backend/helpers.ts requires ../src/aws-exports unconditionally and that file is git-ignored, so a clean checkout fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The repository ships the remedy as its own script; nothing was invented here.

loopbackProbes.reading: the API enforces its session auth on unauthenticated reads

loopbackProbes.request: POST /login with a username from the committed seed document and the seed default password from the committed .env
loopbackProbes.reading: local passport-local authentication succeeded end to end: the credential was checked with bcrypt against the hash in the lowdb seed and a user object was returned with a connect.sid session cookie. No external host was contacted.
the express-graphql endpoint with the loaded schema and resolvers is live

steps.credentialsNote: The username and password used are fixture values from the public repository's own committed seed data and committed .env. They are deliberately not reproduced in this record.

authMode.howSelected: By the absence of every provider variable. src/index.tsx branches on REACT_APP_AUTH0, then REACT_APP_OKTA, then REACT_APP_AWS_COGNITO, then REACT_APP_GOOGLE, and falls through to a final else that renders src/containers/App.tsx. backend/app.ts mirrors this: it always mounts backend/auth.ts, and mounts checkAuth0Jwt / verifyOktaToken / checkCognitoJwt / checkGoogleJwt only when the matching variable is set. The committed .env leaves all four commented out, so `yarn dev` and `yarn start` select local mode with no flags at all.
authMode.mechanism: passport-local + express-session, NOT JWT. POST /login runs passport.authenticate('local'), which looks the username up in the lowdb document and compares the password with bcrypt.compareSync; the session is carried in a connect.sid cookie. The JWT libraries in the closure serve only the four external-provider modes.
authMode.tokenNameVariable: REACT_APP_AUTH_TOKEN_NAME is read by src/machines/authMachine.ts for localStorage token handling and is commented out in .env — it is documented there as being for the external provider modes.

summary.networkDuringBaseline: registry.yarnpkg.com for the package manager's own fetches, plus nodejs.org for the runtime; no application code contacted any host

unknownPreserved: The application was never loaded in a browser by this unit. That the bundle builds and that the API answers on loopback says nothing about whether any journey renders or completes.
The dev-server path (`yarn start` / `react-scripts -r @cypress/instrument-cra start`) was not exercised; only the production build was.
The upstream Cypress suite was not run.
Whether the frozen React adapters can migrate this application is exactly the question this holdout exists to answer, and nothing here answers it.
nonclaims: A successful baseline build establishes that this application compiles in this one cell. It establishes no browser behavior, migration feasibility, pilot status, production readiness, certification, or legal approval.
No adapter, transform, or migration lane is declared for this fixture by the unit that ingested it.
